Subject: Switching billing cadence — exploring annual consolidation and concessions

Hi Monica,

Quick question from procurement here — we’re evaluating consolidating multiple monthly invoices into a single annual prepay for 2027. The finance team asked whether Redwood can:

- Provide tiered discounting for a 1yr vs 2yr commitment
- Offer ramp credits for projected adoption in Q1
- Clarify invoicing cadence and cancellation terms for annualized contracts

Attached is a short RFP extract that calls out expected usage across three product routes. We’d like to understand what concession scenarios Redwood can offer so we can run this through our internal approval.

Can we get a short summary and a sample commercial scenario by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks,
Emma

Hi Emma,

Thanks for the RFP snippet — appreciate the usage breakdown. We can absolutely model a few paths. High level options we typically propose:

1) 1-year annual prepay: 8%-14% term discount depending on committed $ and routes included
2) 2-year annual prepay: an incremental 6% on top of 1yr pricing (so total ~14%-20%) with price protection in year 2
3) Staged annual with ramp credits: give a first-quarter consumption credit (X% of committed value) to account for onboarding lag

Questions that will change the numbers: projected Q1 ramp %, whether you need dedicated capacity (Dedicated) vs hosted, and whether you require private deployment or HIPAA add-ons. Can you confirm the expected first-6-months utilization (low/med/high) for each route?

I’ll pull together two sample commercial scenarios (1yr and 2yr) and include an optional ramp credit structure. Ben and Karthik, tagging you for pricing and legal-level redline considerations.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Emma / Monica,

Quick commercial scenarios attached below as bullets (high level):

- Scenario A (1yr, hosted API): Commit $540k/year (~45k/mo current run-rate) -> 12% discount, no ramp credit. Effective price: $475k/year.
- Scenario B (1yr + ramp): Commit $540k, 8% discount + Q1 ramp credit of $25k applied to invoices if Q1 usage < 25% of committed units.
- Scenario C (2yr protected): Commit $1.02M over 2yrs -> 18% discount applied across year 1/2, 6-month price protection for model variants. $40k onboarding credit in year 1.

Notes/assumptions:
- Dedicated capacity requests add an extra capacity surcharge; we can provide a blended rate if you need guaranteed throughput.
- Ramp credits are one-time true-ups or invoice credits; they do not change committed value for year-end true-up calculations.

If HealthGrid is open to a 2yr commit, we can also include a limited operational SLA uplift and a short-term onboarding services credit. I can put these into a draft SOW and term sheet.

Thanks Ben — that framing is helpful. Procurement prefers Scenario B if we can tighten the ramp credit triggers and get the Q1 credit to apply automatically if onboarding milestones are missed. A couple of clarifying asks from Finance:

- Can you structure the ramp credit so it is an invoice-level credit applied within 30 days (Finance dislikes retrospective true-ups that rely on year-end calculations)?
- For the 2yr offer, what is the refund/cancellation policy if we significantly underutilize in year 2? Finance wants a clear clawback or true-up formula.
- Are there any usage buckets that would qualify for additional discounting (e.g., embedding-heavy usage vs generation-heavy)?

If you can update Scenario B with a tighter Q1 milestone definition and sample credit mechanics, we’ll circulate to Finance and Legal. Also happy to schedule a 30-minute commercial call with our CFO this week.

Emma

Emma, Monica — thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Finalizing a recommended commercial approach below so you have a single proposal to review with Finance/CFO: 

- Proposed: Scenario B (1yr annual prepay with ramp guardrails)
  - Commitment: $540k annual prepay (single invoice)
  - Discount: 10% off list (reflects inclusion of three routes in the commit)
  - Q1 Onboarding / Ramp Credit: $30k invoice credit automatically applied within 30 days if Q1 consumption < 30% of committed units OR if two mutually agreed onboarding milestones are not achieved by day 60.
  - True-up: quarterly usage true-up only if actuals exceed committed units; underutilization does not reduce committed value during the year (standard prepay policy).
  - Cancellation: prorated refund on remaining committed value with 30% administrative charge for early termination in year 1; different for 2yr.
  - Embedding-heavy workloads: qualify for an additional 3% volume discount if embeddings > 60% of total token units for the committed routes.

Next steps:
- Monica & Ben: deliver a 1-page commercial term sheet and a draft SOW (Monica do the term sheet; Ben pull the SOW template).
- Emma: confirm whether HealthGrid wants an initial CFO call (30 min).

I’ll also upload the draft term sheet to HubSpot and share the DocuSign link once we agree the language.
